paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. Jesus withdraws by boat to a solitary place, and a large crowd follows Him on foot anyway. He has compassion on them and heals their sick (Matthew 14:13-14). So when a crowd turns up right where Jesus went to be alone, I see His compassion.

Then the disciples do the math, and the math says send everybody away. It's a sensible plan, and Jesus still says, "They do not need to go away…" and "You give them something to eat." (Matthew 14:16). They show up with five loaves and two fish, and Jesus says, "Bring them here to Me…" (Matthew 14:18). He didn't ask for more first, He asked for what they had.

So here's the big idea, baker. What the disciples had looked small next to what was needed, and Jesus still told them to bring it to Him. He blessed it, broke it, and the disciples gave it to the people, who all ate and were satisfied, with twelve basketfuls left over (Matthew 14:19-20). That's why my ovens stay ready: I keep my little bag of chocolate chips handy and my eyes open for what He does with it!
